articleTitle: Proposal of a Load Shedding Scheme for Microgrids Using IEC 61850 Standard and the Rate of Change of Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The paper presents an adaptive algorithm for a Load Shedding Scheme (LSS), based on the IEC 61850 standard and the Fast Frequency Change Protection (Fast RoCoF). A Python algorithm is developed and implemented in the Spyder environment, facilitating the coordination between renewable and thermal sources in a microgrid modeled in PowerFactory. The microgrid includes non-dispatchable generation such as wind and photovoltaic (PV), and dispatchable generation such as thermal, a battery energy storage system (BESS) and the Electrical Company Network. A communications architecture is established according to the IEC 61850 standard to obtain electrical measurements and send GOOSE messages for automatic load disconnection. In validation, the LSS is evaluated in contingencies such as grid disconnection and loss of a renewable source, improving performance times compared to the traditional LSS.

articleTitle: Performance of PID and NNPID Controllers in a Didactic Pasteurization Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This work focuses on the control of temperature and pressure in a heater-type heat exchanger of a didactic pasteurization plant for fluids with variable viscosity, which affects the control of these variables. The solution to this multivariable control problem is to use a controller that automatically self-tunes proactively using a mathematical model. In a heat exchanger, it is generally desired to maintain a constant output fluid temperature by varying the input temperature or the flow rate of the hot fluid. Other ways to achieve the same objectives include varying the total heat transfer coefficient or the heat transfer area. In this case, the temperature of the glycerin is measured, and the flow rate of the ethylene glycol is adjusted. As stated, the viscosity of glycerin varies inversely with respect to temperature. Consequently, the pressure of the main pump cannot remain constant. This requires pressure control through another frequency converter that will regulate the angular speed of the pump and the pressure of the glycerin. In the plate heat exchanger of the didactic installation at the Thermofluids laboratory of the State University of Milagro (UNEMI), it is possible to implement the strategy of controlling the glycerin temperature by varying the flow rate of the heating fluid (ethylene glycol). In this case, the temperature of the glycerin is measured, and the flow rate of the ethylene glycol is adjusted. The system under study is a Two-Input, Two-Output (TITO) system. The control of TITO systems is designed based on the design requirements of Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems. The main idea of this work is to enhance the capabilities of the classical Proportional, Integral, and Derivative (PID) controller by using Artificial Neural Networks and to conduct a comparative analysis of the performance between the PID and the Neural Network PID (NNPID) controllers. The performance of the designed controllers was verified by simulation using the plant model obtained experimentally. The simulation support for the control strategies was based on the programming and facilities provided by MATLAB and its simulation tool SIMULINK.

articleTitle: Comparison of Sliding Mode Control using different Reaching Laws for a nonlinear pH process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This paper introduces the design of a sliding mode controller employing three distinct reaching laws. These laws are implemented and tested within a nonlinear model of a pH process. The study offers a comprehensive and visual comparison of the key features and effectiveness of each control law by conducting extensive simulations and evaluating multiple performance indices. Given the inherently complex nature of pH processes, this research provides valuable information to use advanced control strategies in similar nonlinear systems.

articleTitle: An IoT System for Monitoring and Controlling Microclimates using Fuzzy Logic Applied to a Vermicompost Culture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Incorporating electronics and technology into agriculture is crucial for optimizing agricultural and livestock production. This study presents the implementation of an Internet of Things (IoT) system with fuzzy logic to monitor and control the microclimate of a vermicompost plot at the Escuela Superior Politécnica de Chimborazo (ESPOCH), adjusting variables such as soil temperature, humidity, and $\mathbf{p H}$. This nonlinear method significantly improves the quality and efficiency of vermicompost production in Ecuador, where manual methods pose challenges regarding time and quality due to the lack of information on environmental variables. The research method involves implementing a fuzzy logic system that collects data through sensors and makes automated decisions displayed in an online system. Using fuzzy logic in IoT systems significantly advances vermicompost research and production, optimizing environmental conditions and reducing reliance on manual control.

articleTitle: Tuning PSO-Based Dynamic Sliding Mode Control for Thermal Process with Long-time Delay
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This paper presents a Dynamic Sliding Mode Control (DSMC) approach designed to reduce the chattering effect commonly observed in conventional Sliding Mode Control (SMC). The controller parameters are optimized using Particle Swarm Optimization. Performance is evaluated using the Integral Squared Error (ISE) and Total Variation of Control Action (TVu) metrics. Results indicate that the SMC controller exhibits substantial chattering, while the DSMC approach significantly mitigates this effect and successfully achieves the desired temperature response in the TCLab long-time delay system during reference tracking, model uncertainty, and disturbance tests.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Convergence and Stability of a Genetic Algorithm Using Different Selection Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Genetic algorithms (GA) are indispensable tools in research, enabling the resolution of intricate optimization challenges across diverse domains. Their capacity to thoroughly explore expansive search spaces and bypass local optima sets them apart from conventional approaches. Widely applied in bio informatics for sequence optimization, in engineering for design optimization, and in machine learning for neural network tuning, genetic algorithms demonstrate remarkable versatility in addressing nonlinear, multi-modal problems. This versatility fuels advancements in scientific and engineering research, rendering genetic algorithms vital for innovation and discovery. This article assesses the stability and convergence of a genetic algorithm used to solve a manufacturing problem, where the goal is to maximize performance based on the operation of a set of machines. The objective is to find the most efficient way to operate 10 machines producing various products, utilizing four distinct selection techniques: Fitness Proportional Selection (FPS), Exponential Rank Selection (ERS), Linear Rank Selection (LRS), and random selection. The algorithm’s performance will be assessed based on the diversity of solutions generated and the convergence patterns observed for each selection method.

articleTitle: Optimization Tool for Energy Management in Hybrid Storage Systems of Isolated Microgrids with Solar PV and Hydrokinetic Turbines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The global transition towards sustainable energy systems has highlighted the importance of renewable resources. Remote Andean regions, particularly in Ecuador, face significant challenges in accessing reliable electricity due to harsh geographical conditions and isolation from the main power grid. This study investigates the integration of photovoltaic (PV) solar and submersible hydrokinetic turbine (HKT) generation systems with hybrid battery energy storage systems consisting of lithiumion and absorbent glass mat valve-regulated lead-acid batteries. An optimization tool is developed to manage these resources effectively, focusing on minimizing operational costs, maximizing renewable energy utilization, and prolonging battery lifespan by reducing charge/discharge cycles. The proposed tool is validated using actual production data from solar PV and HKT systems in the Andean region of Ecuador. The case study demonstrates the tool’s capability to provide a reliable and sustainable electricity supply in remote communities.

articleTitle: Teleoperation of the TurtleBot Mobile Robot using an SMC controller in environments with obstacles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This paper presents the teleoperation of the mobile robot TurtleBot3 Burger in an environment with obstacles, a Sliding Mode Controller (SMC) and a Lyapunov controller are implemented for the velocity control of a mobile robot. The velocity reference is provided by the operator using a joystick. Teleoperation is performed by modifying the velocity reference through mechanical impedance. The velocity error is compensated through the SMC controller to enhance system robustness. Experimental tests are conducted to verify the developed algorithms, and the stability analysis is performed through Lyapunov.

articleTitle: Low Cost Helical and Quadrifilar Helix Antennas in C Band for Tracking UAVs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: In this work, two types of helical antennas, unifilar and quadrifilar for a center frequency of f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>= 5.8 GHz, are presented. The objective was to develop a low cost and low complexity solution; therefore, the antennas were developed in a 3D printer, using a PLA for antennas supports, doorbell wire for the radiating elements and FR4 material for feeding networks. The results show a good performance in return losses in both antennas. The best relative bandwidth obtained was with quadrifilar antenna ($27 \%$) and the best gain with unifilar helical antenna (10 dB). An axial ratio below 3 dB is achieved within the entire $B_{-10 \mathrm{~dB}}$ in both cases, which permits guarantee the circular polarization. Hence, these antennas have good performance in the desired operation band and can be developed for many applications when tracking UAVs.

articleTitle: U-Net Models for Breast Cancer Detection: Improving Diagnostic Accuracy and Specificity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Breast cancer remains a critical global health issue, necessitating continuous research and innovative approaches for diagnosis, treatment, and prevention. This study evaluates the effectiveness of U -Net models in enhancing diagnostic precision and efficiency using real hospital samples. We aim to improve key diagnostic metrics such as accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity through the application of U-Net models. Our image classification model, tailored for $256 \times 256 \times 3$ input images, excels in detecting and categorizing tumor cells. The architecture begins with initial convolutional layers featuring 64 filters, progresses to layers with 128 filters, and includes a Dropout layer to prevent overfitting. The deep network for object detection utilizes both region proposal and regression/classification approaches, achieving $\mathbf{9 2. 2 7 \%}$ confidence and $100 \%$ accuracy. Additionally, our deep learning algorithms accurately segment nuclei in histopathological images, employing a clustering strategy that delivers $88.81 \%$ confidence and $100 \%$ accuracy. Visual results demonstrate precise tumor cell localization and prediction confidence. Performance metrics from ten experimental runs indicate average confidence levels between $\mathbf{7 4. 1 9 \%}$ and $\mathbf{9 2. 3 1 \%}$, with $\mathbf{9 0. 0 \%}$ accuracy and specificity in benign analysis. The model’s ability to classify non-carcinomas versus carcinomas achieved an AUC of 0.78, illustrating its effective differentiation between classes.

articleTitle: iPI Controller for Variable Dead Time Processes: Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Dead time frequently appears in many industrial processes and is a challenge for control systems because of the stability and performance problems that it generates. Various approaches, including controllers based on a process model and model-free controllers, have dealt with the dead time effects. However, classic controllers such as PID can sometimes perform poorly in the presence of long or variable dead time. This study proposes implementing an intelligent Proportional Integral (iPI) controller for nonlinear processes with variable dead time, focusing on a mixing tank application. The implemented iPI controller utilizes data-driven methods and a particle swarm optimization algorithm for controller tuning. To our knowledge, no existing iPID solutions exist for systems with variable dead time, highlighting the novelty of this proposal. The performance of the iPI controller is evaluated and compared against PI and sliding mode controllers. Simulation results show that the iPI controller exhibits performance indexes, such as ISE (integral square error) and ISCO (integral squared of control output), which are better than the PI controller and comparable with sliding mode control. This behavior shows the feasibility of the iPI controller in managing systems with variable dead time, offering promising insights for future control strategies.

articleTitle: Integration of Lego Mindstorms EV3 and MATLAB/Simulink in the Teaching of Robotics and Automation in Manufacturing Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Currently, one of the problems at the high school level is the lack of knowledge about pursuing a specific career, especially for those interested in the field of electronics and automation, which involves robotics and process control. Due to this lack of knowledge, there is often personal demotivation and dropout from the career. The objective of this work is to use the Lego Mindstorm EV3 in teaching robotics and automation in manufacturing processes by implementing a color sorter conveyor belt using Simulink. For the construction of this system, a total of 413 pieces from the kit including sensors and motors were required, which was carried out in three stages: construction stage, programming stage, and communication stage. Additionally, to strengthen technical skills and engineering and programming concepts, a process guide was implemented so that students can step by step implement the color sorter conveyor belt system.

articleTitle: Performance assessment of a Low-Power Wide-Area wireless network based on LoRa technology using IoT devices in different Bolivia areas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This project focuses on the implementation and performance analysis of a Low Power Wide Area Network (LPWAN) using IoT devices in an urban environment. We develop an IoT Node and a Gateway designed to emulate the behavior of a LoRa network architecture. The technical parameters of these devices have been rigorously validated through extensive measurement campaigns and theoretical simulations using advanced radio propagation simulation software. The collected data and simulation results provide a comprehensive assessment of the LoRa technology’s performance, demonstrating its effectiveness and reliability in the specified urban and rural context.

articleTitle: Environmental Sustainability in Industrial Operations: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: As industrial activities expand, their significant environmental impact calls for the adoption of sustainable practices to mitigate adverse effects on ecosystems and communities. This comprehensive review synthesizes recent literature from recognized databases such as Scopus, SciELO, IEEE Xplore and Latindex, focusing on articles published within the last five years that emphasize the implementation of sustainable strategies in industrial operations. Our findings highlight a range of implemented strategies across various sectors, including advancements in energy efficiency through technology integration and resource optimization. Despite these improvements, challenges such as high resource consumption and waste production persist, underscoring the ongoing conflict between industrial growth and environmental preservation. The review discusses case studies demonstrating both the environmental and economic benefits of sustainable practices, illustrating the potential for industry-wide improvements. Conclusively, while the industrial sector has made notable progress towards sustainability, substantial efforts are required to address inherent challenges such as the high costs of initial investments and general resistance to change. Future research should explore the development and application of innovative technologies tailored to specific industrial needs, aiming to foster a holistic approach to sustainability that integrates economic, social, and environmental aspects.

articleTitle: A Simple Solution for an Electromagnetic Wave in a Third-Order Nonlinear Anisotropic Medium
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This work examines how a transverse magnetic mode electromagnetic wave propagates in a medium with thirdorder nonlinear and anisotropic electric permittivity. The proposed model is solved using the homotopy analysis method. Two cases are considered: the first analyzes a wave traveling through an infinite medium, and the results show a transverse rotation of the electric field, indicating that the material induces a change in longitudinal polarization. In the second case, the wave passes through a waveguide with metallic boundaries. The eigenvalues were determined and compared with those of a linear and isotropic material. The results show that nonlinearity and anisotropy eliminate the first eigenvalues, while, for large eigenvalues, both materials exhibit the same values.

articleTitle: Understanding Student Sentiment in Teacher Evaluations Using Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This study focuses on the inherent complexity of teaching evaluation analysis and understanding at the university level. We propose an approach that merges traditional evaluation methods with advanced natural language processing (NLP) techniques, in particular, sentiment analysis and Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA). We seek to improve the interpretation of comments given by students, overcoming the challenges associated with vast amounts of unstructured data. The innovative use of NLP techniques in the field of teaching evaluation allows not only for positive and negative opinion categorization but also, to identify latent thematic patterns which may further provide a deeper understanding of student perceptions and biases.

articleTitle: Design and Construction of an Internal Combustion Engine Go-Kart as an Educational Tool
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This paper presents the design and construction of a Go-Kart powered by an internal combustion engine, developed as an educational tool to enhance hands-on learning in mechanical engineering. The project aims to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application, providing students with a comprehensive understanding of automotive principles and mechanical systems. During the design stage, extensive considerations were given to ergonomics, safety, and performance. Advanced Computer-Aided Design (CAD) software, specifically 3D Autodesk Inventor, was used to create detailed and accurate models of the Go-Kart chassis and components. Besides, iterative design processes, including stress analysis, ensured the structural integrity and durability of the chassis, with a particular focus on the Von Mises stress analysis to validate the safety factor. Results shows that the Go-Kart met all design specifications and performed reliably. This project not only proves the feasibility of constructing a functional Go-Kart but also significantly contribute to the educational development of students. It facilitates interdisciplinary collaboration, applies method design theories, and provides valuable hands-on experience in both virtual and real-world settings. The integration of practical projects into the engineering curriculum has shown to increase student engagement and interest in STEM fields. The paper concludes with an analysis of the project outcomes, highlighting the educational impact and practical skills gained.

articleTitle: Integrating Collaborative Online International Learning in Applied Biomechanics Education
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The Pontificia Universidad Católica del Perú in Lima and the Instituto Tecnológico Metropolitano of Medellín, Colombia, offer a Biomedical Engineering program. Since 2018, both institutions have collaborated on various projects, with a recent highlight being the development of a Collaborative Online International Learning (COIL) course for the subject of Biomechanics. In a context where global trends in education emphasize the importance of internationalization, interdisciplinary teaching, and active learning, the COIL methodology emerges as an innovative tool to addresses these needs. By integrating students and faculty from different cultures, COIL facilitates a synergy of knowledge that maximizes interdisciplinary learning and promotes the practical application of theoretical concepts to solve real-world problems, enriching the participants’ professional and academic development. The COIL course in Biomechanics covers key areas such as anthropometry, clinical biomechanics, occupational biomechanics, and sports biomechanics. It utilizes laboratories and academic projects that allow students to apply their knowledge in practical scenarios. The course assessment focuses not only on theoretical knowledge but also on students’ ability to solve problems, work in teams, and apply their skills in real-world contexts, with continuous feedback supporting their professional growth. The course results show high satisfaction among students, with over $\mathbf{8 0 \%}$ expressing favorability toward the enriching experience of international exchange. From an academic perspective, it has been observed that the course tends to generate a higher level of rigor for students. Although technical and communication challenges arose, suggestions for improvement include increasing practical activities, enhancing technology, and further encouraging students’ participation.

articleTitle: Experimental performance analysis of a low complexity 20 Gb/s PAM4-PON based on legacy 10G hardware
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This paper presents the experimental performance analysis of a $20 \mathrm{~Gb} / \mathrm{s}$ PAM4-PON which was deployed using 10 G legacy electrical and optical hardware. It studied the behavior of the BER vs the decrement of the received optical power on the ONU side and the behavior of the optical path penalty. The test results of the $20 \mathrm{~Gb} / \mathrm{s}$ PON were contrasted with the performance of a traditional $10 \mathrm{~Gb} / \mathrm{s}$ PAM2-NRZ PON. With a received optical power of -10 dBm it was possible to achieve a BER of $10^{-9}$ with the PAM4-PON, whilst in a PAM2-NRZ PON the same BER is achievable when a signal of $\mathbf{- 1 9} \mathrm{dBm}$ is received in the ONU. The optical path penalty of the PAM4 is greater than 2.5 dB when the optical link length is close to 30 km, but it is very low when the ODN is shorter than 25 km.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Domestic Wastewater Treatment Plants Employing Eichhornia crassipes Biofilters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Floating plant-based wastewater treatment systems have gained recognition as effective approaches for remediating a diverse range of contaminants in water, encompassing nutrients, organic matter, and toxic substances such as arsenic, zinc, cadmium, copper, lead, chromium, and mercury. Their primary advantage lies in their suitability for rural areas due to their low consumption of conventional energy and the simplicity of construction and operation. This research delved into the incorporation of Eichhornia crassipes, locally known as “Lechuguin,” into biofilters for domestic wastewater treatment. A scaled-down prototype of the actual treatment system was constructed to emulate its performance and evaluate its efficacy in nutrient removal. The primary objective was to reduce pollutant parameter levels below permissible limits before discharging the treated effluent into a receiving water body. The behavior of floating lechuguines in the biofilter was analyzed, considering general aspects such as the advantages and disadvantages of employing these plants for wastewater depuration. The results obtained demonstrated favorable outcomes in some water quality parameters, while others were inconclusive.

articleTitle: Family functioning and social network addiction in college students of the city of Quito
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This research aims to analyze the relationship between family functioning and social network addiction in college students in the city of Quito. The research design is nonexperimental cross-sectional, with a quantitative method and a descriptive - correlative scope. Two data collection instruments are used: 1. Social Networks Addiction Questionnaire (ARS) and 2. Family Functioning Perception Questionnaire (FF-SIL). The sample consisted of 274 college students from the city of Quito. The results were $50 \%$ of moderately functional families, in addition to a higher prevalence of students with an “obsession to be informed” and a “need/obsession to be connected” with $\mathbf{5 1. 8 \%}$ and $\mathbf{4 2. 3 \%}$ respectively. Likewise, there is a statistically significant correlation, directly proportional between family functioning and the “problem” dimension of social networks addiction.

articleTitle: 3D Reconstruction of a Tomato Seed Germination Environment Using LiDAR and Color Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: In this work, the process of recreating a seedling cultivation environment in three dimensions through the acquisition of coordinates presented via point clouds using a LiDAR sensor and a color camera was investigated. The process is highlighted by the versatility of movement provided by a Cartesian robot, which operates along the X and Y axes. For data acquisition and processing, software was developed in Python, and the captured images were merged with a PLY file that can be visualized in Open3D in Python. The analysis of the final reconstruction results emphasizes the importance of integrating technologies to obtain detailed information about the seedling bed. Multiple tests were conducted to analyze the effects of lighting and terrain conditions on the quality of the data, particularly the height data collected during the analysis. This innovative approach is capable of optimizing the planting process and promoting the healthy growth of plants in a controlled environment.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of Internal Model Control Using Reduced Fractional Order Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The aim of this paper is a comparison of three different Internal Model Control (IMC) based on the obtained reduced models; the control structure is formulated in the internal model control (IMC) framework. Two reduced order models, an FOPDT and a FOFOPDT model. The three IMC controllers are one with a whole order, one-half fractional, and the other a complete fractional one. The idea is to apply them in a nonlinear system with variable and dominant delay for tracking and disturbances rejection to observe how the fractional terms improve or not the performance.

articleTitle: Organizational Commitment in Savings and Credit Cooperatives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: With globalization and technological advancements, companies face changes that require a culture of continuous learning and adaptation. The changes effectively managing can determine an organization’s success in a dynamic environment. Organizational Commitment (OC) is crucial as it measures employees’ identification, belonging, and loyalty. In Ecuador, savings and credit unions and non-profit financial institutions decreased from 817 active entities in 2015 to 408 in 2023, functioning as an important source of employment. It is essential to determine the OC level and analyze its variables. Therefore, a bibliometric review was conducted to identify the scientific production on the subject, followed by a systematic review to substantiate and identify methods for measuring OC. The Meyer and Allen scale test was applied to 169 employees of a cooperative union. The data was processed using SPSS to perform a descriptive and correlational analysis with a non-experimental, cross-sectional design. The sample was evenly split between men and women, revealing connections between study dimensions and areas for improvement..

articleTitle: Color Classification Using a 3-DOF Robotic Arm Based on the YOLOv5 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The combination of robotic arms and computer vision has greatly enhanced the efficiency and accuracy of object classification tasks across multiple industries. This work proposes the implementation of a 3-degree-of-freedom robotic arm designed for classifying objects by color using the YOLOv5 deep-learning model. Traditionally, object classification has been addressed through manual sorting or basic automated systems with limited accuracy. Our approach employs YOLOv5s for real-time color detection and provides the flexibility of automatic operation as well as remote control via radiofrequency. The system builds on recent developments in robotics and computer vision to enhance sorting accuracy. During testing, the model achieved 87% precision, demonstrating effective object classification and manipulation by the robotic arm. These results suggest significant potential for improving automation in color-based sorting

articleTitle: Mechatronic Development of a Delta Robot Applied to MPS 500
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This document is a description of the design and implementation of a delta robot model with position control. The mechanical design of the prototype is based on the requirements of the workspace, with a structural analysis that guarantees the coverage of the required area and the strength of the materials used.From the inverse kinematic analysis, a joint position control system is proposed based on a proportional, integral and derivative (PID) controller, designed to adapt to the programmed conditions of the mechanism. This control system is implemented in a programming interface developed in Python®.After the implementation phase, tests are carried out to evaluate the effectiveness and performance of the robot. These tests are based on error indicators, using the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) as the main indicator to quantify the difference between the desired positions and the positions reached by the robot.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of a Simulation-Based Bioelectricity Practice in Medical Education
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Simulation-based medical education has proved to be an essential element of medical training, offering realistic and controlled environments for students to develop clinical skills. This study evaluates the effectiveness of a simulation-based bioelectricity practice in enhancing medical students’ knowledge, skills, and confidence. A quasi-experimental prepost design was employed, involving Thirty-three second-semester medical students who were divided into 11 groups. The study measured students’ understanding of bioelectric concepts, confidence in using a defibrillator, and teamwork coordination during cardiac emergencies through pre-test and post-test assessments and a checklist evaluation. Results indicated significant improvements in all areas measured. Post-test scores revealed increased confidence in using a defibrillator and enhanced ability to describe electrical concepts. Checklist performance showed an average score of $80 / 100$, with the highest scores in the appropriate use of bioelectricity terms. However, identification and proper selection of monitoring and defibrillation materials were identified as areas needing improvement. The findings align with existing literature on the benefits of simulation-based education, highlighting its role in preparing students for real-life medical emergencies. This study underscores the importance of integrating high-fidelity simulations into medical curriculum to improve learning outcomes. Future research should explore the long-term retention of skills acquired through simulation training and the potential of advanced simulation technologies.

articleTitle: Design of a Lithium-Ion Battery Pack for an Electric Two-Seater Vehicle.
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This study designs a battery pack for a two-seater electric vehicle using lithium iron phosphate technology, to replace lead-acid gel batteries. By comparing the performance, range, and weight of both battery types through simulations and modeling, the research finds that lithium iron phosphate batteries provide better performance, longer range, and are lighter. They also maintain optimal temperatures in hot coastal areas and have a lower environmental impact than lead-acid batteries.

articleTitle: Learning in Multivariable Control Using Coupled Tanks: Design, Construction, and Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This work aims to provide undergraduate students with practical experience in designing and implementing multivariable control systems. A laboratory setup was created to facilitate real-time simulation and testing, focusing on the Coupled Tank Process, which involves controlling water levels in two connected tanks using two pumps. The system was assembled using basic materials and standard instrumentation, with a Human-Machine Interface (HMI) developed in Matlab for realtime control. The setup incorporates the Relative Gain Array, making it an effective educational tool to teach the fundamentals of multivariable control. The research provides a basis for future exploration of advanced control techniques.

articleTitle: An IoT-Based Measurement Device for E-bike Tracking Performance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Electric bicycles (e-bikes) have emerged as a promising solution to meet urban mobility needs efficiently and sustainably. However, for e-bikes to fulfill their role in sustainable mobility, it is essential to analyze and understand their energy consumption. This work aims to address this issue by developing an IoT device for data acquisition and processing from e-bike sensors. The methodology employed in this study involves the selection and integration of sensors, as well as the integration of the bike’s intrinsic network, software development for Iot devices (ESP32, Thingsboard, and Android), PCB design for component interconnection, and the configuration of Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and GPS communications for data collection, storage, and transmission. The obtained results were validated through comparisons with reference measurement instruments and commercial devices, demonstrating accuracy and consistency in the measurements. The study highlights the viability and benefits of e-bikes in terms of energy efficiency, reduced operating costs, and lower environmental impact compared to conventional motor vehicles. This work lays the groundwork for future research and improvements in the field of e-bikes and the optimization of their energy consumption.

articleTitle: Exploring New Frontiers in Concrete Compression Test with Augmented Reality
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The compression test for concrete specimens measures the maximum compression resistance a concrete element can withstand in actual construction. For this, 21-day-old concrete samples were prepared and subjected to axial force using a universal testing machine until failure occurred. These failures are explosive and unexpected, happening in a short time, which allows for careful analysis of the material’s behavior. The tests were recorded using 2 video cameras and 1 thermography.The research aims to incorporate new technologies, such as augmented reality, into traditional lab tests, focusing on temperature variation and resistance. This approach allows for archiving the tests in augmented reality, enabling multiple views from different angles, slow-motion analysis, and image enlargement. This helps in understanding the material’s behavior at the exact moment of failure and could also include additional data like stress, deformation, and other future requirements.

articleTitle: Multi-Area Power System Frequency Regulation based Coordinated Control of SMES Farms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Power systems and their components are susceptible to frequency and voltage instability during disturbances, affecting critical sectors such as industry, transportation, medicine, and banking. This study introduces a phasor model of a Superconducting Magnetic Energy Storage System (SMES) with intelligent fuzzy logic-based control for frequency regulation using SMES system farms. The SMES model allows for simultaneous and independent control of reactive and active power injected into or absorbed from the grid. Frequency measurements are acquired via Virtual Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs), which are utilized to calculate the Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF). This value is then input into a fuzzy control system to coordinate the energy injection or absorption from the SMES farms. Finally, two SMES farms are integrated into the IEEE 39-Bus New England system to improve frequency stability during disturbances caused by load disconnection and generation tripping. This work is a continuation of the methodologies presented in [2] and [3].

articleTitle: Precision Agriculture: Enhancing Crops and Weeds Classification of Unbanlance Databases via Weighted-Loss Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: In the realm of precision agriculture, accurately distinguishing between crops and weeds is essential for optimizing yield and minimizing resource use. This study explores the efficacy of weighted-loss functions in handling unbalanced datasets for image classification in agricultural applications. We conducted experiments under three distinct training scenarios: data augmentation without weightedloss, data augmentation with weighted-loss, and weighted-loss without data augmentation. Our findings reveal that while data augmentation alone yielded an overall accuracy of $\mathbf{9 7. 2 0 \%}$, it failed to address the unbalanced class, resulting in misclassification of the carrot class. Incorporating a weighted-loss function with data augmentation slightly improves the classification accuracy of the unbalanced class, reducing the misclassification error. The most notable improvement was observed when using a weighted-loss function without data augmentation, achieving a validation accuracy of $99.20 \%$ and enhancing the unbalanced class accuracy from $66.67 \%$ without weighted-loss to $88.89 \%$ with weighted-loss. These results underscore the potential of weighted-loss functions in improving model performance on unbalanced agricultural datasets, highlighting their importance in precision agriculture applications.

articleTitle: Development of an IoT system prototype for the acquisition of biomechanical data of a speed skater
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This project addresses performance enhancement in speed skating through the utilization of emerging technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT) and Wearable devices. Currently, the scientific literature in this domain is limited, relying primarily on athletes and coaches as key sources of knowledge to refine techniques. The implementation of measurement systems with inertial sensors is proposed to quantify athlete movements, facilitating more precise training. A wireless IoT system is developed using ESP32 modules and inertial sensors to capture limb acceleration data from the skater. Data are stored on the Thingsboard Cloud Web server using the MQTT protocol. The system architecture comprises a central node and four sensor nodes, communicating via ESP-NOW. In addition, an Android mobile application is created to show data capture and visualize inertial information. The tests were carried out with three skaters with varying level of experience, allowing the characterization of limb acceleration data on straight and curved sections of the track.

articleTitle: Low-complexity Dual Voltage Level Circuitry For Voltage-Divider-Based Content-Addressable Memory (CAM) Based On Two Supply Voltages
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Content addressable memories have raised great interest involving the realm of Big Data and Artificial Intelligence, along with the emerging non-volatile (eNV) technology magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) devices capabilities, they are exploited for massive parallel search operations through (NV-CAMs). A voltage-divider-based NV-BCAM/TCAM has been previously proposed, showing promising characteristics and potential for reliable search operations. Nevertheless, the NV-BCAM relies on two voltage levels to perform write and search operations and does not take into account its periphery design. Hence, the proposed paper presents an NV-BCAM Dual Voltage Level Circuitry design, based on a full-custom methodology, that relies on a low-complexity Voltage-Mode Selector (VMS). Sizing analysis along with Monte Carlo simulations were performed for the designed periphery. In particular, the proposed dual voltage level circuitry will allow for the control of search and write operations in the NV-BCAM memory, delivering $V_{w r i t e}=V_{D D}$ and $V_{{search }}=0.6 {~V}$ through a single voltage supply $\left(V_{D D}=1.1 {~V}\right)$ and further reducing the top-level complexity design.

articleTitle: Predictive Maintenance in Industrial Robotics Using Big Data: Techniques, Challenges, and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: In industrial robotics, predictive maintenance is important to improve efficiency and reduce costs, addressing early detection and diagnosis of failures. The use of Big Data allows us to identify patterns and trends that at first glance are complex. This review examines research on the application of big data in predictive maintenance of industrial robots, which use advanced techniques such as cloud-based architectures, filtering algorithms, and machine learning. The review methodology included an analysis of the big data techniques used, the challenges identified, and the opportunities presented. The results show significant improvements in the accuracy of predictions and fault diagnoses. Key anomaly drivers were identified that improved production performance and enabled accurate fault identification and reduced downtime in industrial robots. Despite the benefits, challenges remain in data security and communications latency, underscoring the need to develop innovative algorithms and techniques to balance computing load and minimize delays. The continuous evolution of these techniques promises to improve the failure management capacity in industrial robotics, thus optimizing the operability and efficiency of robotic systems.

articleTitle: Comparison of Charging and Discharging Behavior of Lithium-Ion Electric Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This work focuses on analyzing and comparing the behavior of lithium-ion electric batteries during the charging and discharging processes, taking into account the degradation effects imposed by the repetition of these cycles. Various models of lithium-ion batteries found in the scientific literature are examined, and the model that directly relates the chemical formulation to the equivalent electrical circuit, along with the charging and discharging operation, as well as the battery degradation process, is selected. The model used is represented by integrating its state variables in both the MATLAB®tool and the graphical environment ATPDraw, using circuits, TACs, and MODELS language. The simulation results are compared with experimental measurements, and conclusions are drawn based on the obtained results.

articleTitle: Distributed State Estimation Through Nodal Redundancy in EPS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This research work proposes a robust methodology for partitioning electrical systems within the distributed estimation framework, using the principle of nodal redundancy. The approach employs measurements from the electrical system’s nodes. This method’s application involves a comparative analysis between centralized estimation and the proposed technique, using the IEEE 14-bus system as the benchmark. The findings underscore the efficacy of the quality of the estimation and the computational efficiency achieved through this novel methodology.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Studies of Large-Signal Salient Pole Synchronous Machines (SPSM) using ATP-EMTP and MODELS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This paper presents the analysis of large-signal transient stability in salient pole synchronous machines (SPSM) using the ATP-EMTP tool and its graphical environment ATPDraw. The machine models were developed using programming in MODELS, and various disturbances in the power system were analyzed, such as single-phase, two-phase, and three-phase short circuits, as well as sudden load changes, to evaluate the dynamic response of the system. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of these tools in simulating and evaluating transient stability, providing valuable information for improving the design and operation of the power system.

articleTitle: Intelligent Control Algorithm Based on Fuzzy Logic for Level Control of a Conical Tank
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The conical tanks, due to their conical shape, allow avoiding sedimentation and reduction of bacteria that frequently occur in conventional tanks. The level control of a conical tank is challenging due to its non-uniform shape. In this research, an algorithm based on fuzzy logic is designed and implemented for the level control of a conical tank at a laboratory scale. To evaluate the controller’s performance, it is compared with a traditional Proportional-Integral (PI) controller, analyzing settling time, overshoot, and steady-state error under different set points, and evaluating the system when subjected to disturbances. The results showed better performance of the fuzzy logic control in the transient state. Additionally, an interactive graphical interface is developed that allows experimenting with the dynamic response of the actual plant when implementing a fuzzy controller.

articleTitle: Methodology for Energy Dispatch in Off-Grid Micro-grids Using Stochastic Analysis of NCRE
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This research focuses on the implementation of an innovative methodology for energy dispatch in micro grids that operate independently from the main power grid. The proposed methodology involves using the results of stochastic analysis of NCRE as input data, which are then fed into the proposed MILP model for optimal dispatch. The novelty of this work lies in optimizing through various scenarios involving PV, wind, BESS, and SOC for energy dispatch, achieving efficient and adaptive management of NCRE across different time windows for the offgrid micro grid. By analyzing a scenario of a regular weekday and holiday over a 48 -hour window, where it is constrained that the BESS starts fully charged. The total cost given by the MILP objective function shows the lowest cost with a value of ${\$}$10.031. In contrast, if the BESS starts fully discharged, the total cost within the same time window and with the same NCRE resources decreases by 31.602 % for the economic dispatch of the off-grid micro grid. This verifies the importance of analyzing various scenarios with different conditions in the available NCRE resources.

articleTitle: Development of a Linear Algebra-Based Controller for a Three-Tank System in Series within a Virtual Reality Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The use of a control method based on linear algebra for a system consisting of three tanks connected in series within a virtual reality setting is the main topic of this paper. The user-friendly virtual environment offers all the tools and infrastructure needed to enable interaction between the user and the industrial process. This includes the ability to simulate the process and control and monitor variables in real-time. This control model has the advantage of using discrete equations, making its implementation possible for most systems. The system model is estimated using numerical methods for the controller design, and a system of linear equations is then solved by least squares. Because of its advancements in technology, realism, and intuitiveness, virtual reality has become an invaluable educational tool. The simulation results created using the Matlab program and Unity multiplatform demonstrate the efficiency of the control algorithm and the system that was put into place. Through interactive tests, the operator can experience an industrial process firsthand and interact with the virtual environment.

articleTitle: Feasibility study using descriptive statistics for the development of a C++ language to block diagram translator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The research work is focused on the development of a bidirectional translation tool between $\mathrm{C}++$ and block diagrams focused on PLC programming, maintaining a semantic equivalence between the two languages, compatibility with different standards, with the objective of integrating a software that meets the current needs in the industry guaranteeing the robustness and recursion that a software demands, the importance of conducting this feasibility study through statistical analysis and surveys is to evaluate the market demand, the most common use of programming languages and the technical, economic and operational feasibility before developing the translation tool. The research employs a mixed quantitative and qualitative approach, the methodology in determining the variables, using techniques and instruments such as data analysis and survey people from various industrial sectors in Ecuador for data collection and analysis with statistical analysis technique. The results obtained by analyzing the data show the feasibility of the bidirectional translation tool with a confidence level of 95 percent, it was also possible to determine data such as programming experience in the two languages, most used equipment, reliable low work experience in the industry, according to age and level of education.

articleTitle: Relaxing Sensing Margins in Double-Barrier Magnetic Tunnel Junction for Energy-Efficient Smart Material Implication (SIMPLY) Scheme Operating at 77K
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This paper explores the impact on reliability and energy-efficiency in double-barrier magnetic tunnel junctions (DMTJs)-based smart material implication (SIMPLY) scheme operating at cryogenic temperatures (77 K). Our study is carried out through a macrospin-based Verilog-A compact model of DMTJ, along with a 65 nm commercial process design kit (PDK) calibrated down to 77 K under silicon measurements. This study evaluates the effects of adjusting the bias voltage. Energy-efficient SIMPLY operations can be achieved by relaxing the bias voltage, and thereby the read sensing margins. DMTJ-based SIMPLY and sFALSE schemes allows energy savings of about $29.2 \%$ and $35 \%$, respectively. We then utilized the SIMPLY and sFALSE logic schemes to assess energy savings in logic operations. These results indicate that DMTJ-based cells under cryogenic conditions are a promising alternative for logic-in-memory (LiM) architectures.

articleTitle: Nanobubbles Generation System for Bacteria Removal in Water through Hydrodynamic Cavitation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Hydrodynamic cavitation is emerging as a sustainable solution for clean water, offering a by-product-free treatment method. Where the formation and collapse of bubbles is used for the degradation and cleaning of contaminants. This article investigates the elimination of Escherichia coli (E. coli) bacteria through the implementation of a hydrodynamic cavitation system composed of static mixers, Venturi tubes and perforated plates. The findings show that an initial concentration of $84 \mathrm{CFU} / \mathrm{mL}$ after a period of 50 minutes was $0 \mathrm{CFU} / \mathrm{mL}$. This implies total sanitation of contaminated water. This technology reveals an important biocidal power, which makes it very effective in the purification and disinfection of liquids. Bacterial cell membranes faced weakening and death due to the combined mechanical and chemical effects of cavitation. The study also examines the benefits and limitations of the cavitation system in practice.

articleTitle: Low-Power Two-Stage Miller-Compensated Operational Amplifier for On-chip Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Emerging wearable devices for biomedical applications and Lab on a Chip (LoC) are rapidly expanding in the electronic market. These devices integrate CMOS-based biosensors for monitoring, measuring and manipulating biochemical reactions in the same system. Biomedical signals and biosensor outputs typically operate at frequencies below 1 kHz and have amplitudes in the $\mu \mathrm{V}$ range. These systems are crucial for low-frequency signal processing in biomedical, biophysical, and biochemical applications. To meet the stringent power constraints of battery-operated wearable devices, the design of analog components like operational amplifiers (OpAmps) must prioritize low power consumption, compact size, and high performance. This paper presents a subthreshold-biased OpAmp design optimized for low-power operation in TSMC $0.18 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ technology. Leveraging subthreshold biasing and Miller compensation techniques, the OpAmp achieves a DC gain of 63 dB with a power consumption of 49 nW and a supply voltage of 1 V. Post-layout simulations confirm stable operation with a phase margin of 64.4° and a gain-bandwidth product of 12.6 kHz. These results demonstrate the OpAmp’s suitability for accurate amplification and processing of low-amplitude and low-frequency biomedical signals.

articleTitle: Performance of Bus Differential Protection due to Electromagnetic and Electrostatic Induction Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: In parallel transmission lines (TLs), electrical and magnetic couplings between conductors and circuits generate induced voltages and currents. When one circuit of the TLs is grounded, a ground-induced current circulates. Based on the operating principle of the bus differential protection (87B), the differential current ($I_{D I F F}$) becomes nonzero when this ground-induced current is considered. This condition is particularly critical in the case of an external fault, where the performance of the 87B protection may be compromised.This paper presents the mathematical expressions for calculating induced voltages and currents and proposes an expression for induced voltages based on sequence quantities. Practical case studies are conducted to verify the performance of 87B protection, considering the grounding of a parallel TL using the proposed expressions and their comparison with simulation results. The study is performed in a zone of the Ecuadorian Transmission System (ETS) and considers both high and low impedance 87B algorithms.

articleTitle: Lyapunov Approach for Load-Frequency Control in Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This work proposes a Load-Frequency Control (LFC) on power system based on a Lyapunov Controller. The developed controller incorporates a speed-droop characteristic to enable its application in a multigenerator system and its operation in conjunction with the secondary regulation performed by Automatic Generation Control (AGC). The proposed controller exhibits good performance and the simulation results in a three-area power system confirm its superiority over the traditional governor-based control.

articleTitle: Telemetry System for Wind Turbines Case Study: University of Cuenca’s Irquis Mini-Wind Farm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Renewable energy systems, like wind energy, require efficient m anagement a nd t imely i nformation f or operators. Monitoring and visualizing data from these systems is crucial in both industrial and residential settings. Telemetry systems are ideal for this, offering real-time information to quickly address and correct failures, streamline procedures, and optimize performance. Thus, telemetry maximizes renewable energy resource use and ensures optimal system operation. This project aims to develop a telemetry system for visualizing and monitoring wind variables for the Micro-Grid laboratory at the University of Cuenca. Data from inverters at the Irquis mini-wind farm is sent to a Thingsboard server via HTTPs. This information can be exported in plain text format for further analysis or future applications. Data received on the Thingsboard display panel was compared with real-time information from each inverter to validate the telemetry system. This ensured the creation of a functional system with real-time data visualization.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Convergence and Stability of a Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm: Application to the Vessel Design Optimization Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is a metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by collective behaviors in nature. This article examines the performance of PSO by considering three methods for adapting the inertia weight: the constriction method, the Random Inertia Weight Method (RIWM), and the Linearly Decreasing Inertia Weight Method (LDIWM). The study addresses a complex optimization problem due to its constraints, specifically focusing on optimizing the manufacturing cost of a pressure vessel. The performance of PSO is measured in terms of convergence and stability. In this way, it is determined which of the three methods achieves greater precision and how often this precision level can be consistently reached. The results demonstrate that the inertia weight is a hyperparameter that significantly impacts the convergence of the PSO algorithm. Therefore, for a given problem, a thorough analysis must be conducted to achieve optimal results.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of an NG-PON Using IM-DD and Complex Modulation and Coherent Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This paper presents a Passive Optical Network (PON) performance analysis using modulation schemes based on amplitude and complex modulation. This research uses the simulation software OptiSystem in co-simulation with Matlab. Data transmitted at 50 and 100 Gbps employ four-level Pulse Amplitude Modulation (PAM-4) and 4-level Phase Shift Keying (Q-PSK) schemes. The results are presented in graphs corresponding to the relationship of Bit Error Rate (BER) and reception power for scenarios of different lengths and attenuation values, supported by constellation diagrams and eye diagrams, which show the performance of the Next Generation Passive Optical Networks(NG-PON).

articleTitle: Comparison of Flexible Substrates for Microstrip Antenna Design for ISM Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: In this paper was made a comparison between three microstrip antennas with different flexible substrates at 2.4 GHz. These substrates are Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET), Thermoplastic Polyurethane (TPU), and a semi-flexible substrate composed by Polyethylene Terephthalate Glycolmodified (PETG). The measurements were focused on parameters of reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>), VSWR, bandwidth (BW), and impedance (Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>). The three models were designed in Ansys HFSS, and for the construction we used 3D prints and copper tape. For S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>, PETG had an improvement of -23.36 dB, and-19.88 dB, in comparison with PET and TPU respectively. For bandwidth, TPU had an improvement of 86,23 MHz and 88 MHz in comparison with PET and PETG respectively. Finally, for VSWR, PETG has an improvement of 0.44 and 0.22 in comparison with PET and TPU. This means that PETG as a semi-flexible material shows better performance in the global scenario of analysis.

articleTitle: Production Optimization in Plastic Packaging Plant: Lean Manufacturing Operational Excellence Model.
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This proposal focuses on the implementation of the operational excellence management model based on Lean Manufacturing in a plastic packaging manufacturing plant to improve the efficiency and quality of the production processes. The model contributes positively to the challenges faced by the company under study, through the implementation of key indicators, training that adds value to the operation, and implementation of Lean tools and principles. In addition, the model presents impacts on overall plant efficiency, including significant reductions in mold changeovers, reduced waiting times, order and cleanliness at workstations, and improved product quality. The economic results impacted by the model were around ${\$}$100,000 after six months, contributing directly to the company’s financial status. Finally, it is concluded that this implementation proposal based on an operational excellence management model contributes significantly to the efficiency and quality of production processes and that the methodology described can be replicated in other companies in the plastic packaging manufacturing sector to obtain similar benefits.

articleTitle: Early Diagnosis of Pancreatic Cancer using Urinary Biomarkers and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Diagnosing pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and chronic pancreatitis (CP) early is crucial for better patient outcomes. However, the lack of specific biomarkers makes this challenging. This study investigated the potential of a panel of four urinary biomarkers (creatinine, LYVE1, REG1B, and TFF1) combined with machine learning (support vector machines and neural networks) for diagnosis. We analyzed a publicly available dataset of 590 urine samples categorized as healthy, benign pancreatic disease, or PDAC. All samples were collected before treatment and age and sex were balanced across groups. Both machine learning models achieved high accuracy (>89%) and sensitivity (>84%) for PDAC diagnosis. For CP diagnosis, neural networks performed slightly better (accuracy: 75.3%, sensitivity: 65.1%) compared to support vector machines (accuracy: 71.0%, sensitivity: 59.0%). These results suggest that both methods hold promise for diagnosing these diseases. The use of urinary biomarkers offers several advantages. Urine collection is non-invasive and patient-friendly, the biomarkers are stable and detectable in early stages of disease, and measurement is relatively inexpensive. Our study has limitations, including a small sample size and a retrospective design. Further research with larger, more diverse populations and prospective studies is needed. Additionally, the potential use of these biomarkers for risk stratification and disease progression monitoring requires investigation. In conclusion, this study demonstrates the potential of a combined approach using urinary biomarkers and machine learning algorithms for diagnosing PDAC and CP. While neural networks showed a slight edge for CP diagnosis, both methods performed well. Further research is needed to validate these findings and explore the broader potential of these biomarkers.

articleTitle: Enhancing Transient Stability in Power Systems with PV-STATCOM: Mitigating the Impact of Photovoltaic Generation Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This paper analyzes the transient stability (TS) of a power system that undergoes a utility-scale replacement of its conventional generation matrix with photovoltaic generation (PVG). In response to the reduction in the oscillation damping capability of the system, this paper also proposes the design and implementation of a power system stabilizer (PSS) in the reactive control loop of photovoltaic system converters as PV-STATCOM mode. The particle swarm optimization (PSO) based method was used to tune the PSS, leveraging its parallel computing capability with MATLAB and Simulink. The results obtained after the replacement of the generation matrix show a deterioration in damping capacity, which is satisfactorily mitigated by the implementation of the PSS.

articleTitle: Impact of Distributed Energy Resources with Photovoltaic Self-Consumption on an Electrical Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The sustainability of electrical distribution networks is essential for ensuring reliable supply and minimizing environmental impact. This study focuses on analyzing the impact of Distributed Energy Resources with photovoltaic selfconsumption systems on a real electrical distribution network, aiming to identify the benefits and challenges these systems present. The methodology employed includes collecting energy consumption data, selecting candidates for the implementation of photovoltaic systems, and modeling and simulating load flows using CYMDIST software. Data collection was carried out in an electric utility company in Ecuador, identifying users with the highest probability of adopting these systems. Subsequently, the photovoltaic systems were modeled in the electrical network, and the technical impacts were evaluated. The results show that the integration of photovoltaic systems alleviates the load on the distribution network, decreases energy losses, and facilitates a more flexible and adaptive management of energy demand. Finally, it is concluded that photovoltaic systems are expected to be a strong base for the transition towards a more sustainable and resilient electricity system.

articleTitle: Comparison of Constant Envelope and Peak Insertion Schemes for PAPR Reduction in a 6G Waveform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: In this paper, we present a comparison between constant envelope (CE) and peak insertion (PI) schemes for the reduction of the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) in multicarrier signal orthogonal frequency division multiplexing with index modulation (OFDM-IM), that was proposed for the sixth-generation wireless networks (6 G). The parameters of the modulation index and the amplitude peak were evaluated, for maximum PAPR reduction, using simulations. A decrease of 7.6 dB is found for the constant envelope scheme for a index modulation of 0.1, which is 0.45 dB more than the peak insertion scheme when the gain of amplitude peak was 200. However, the latter requires a very high power increase over OFDM-IM to achieve this level of reduction. This makes the constant envelop scheme suitable for future green wireless networks.

articleTitle: Low-Code/No-Code Meets GenAI: A New Era in Product Development
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This paper focuses on the convergence of Low-Code/No-Code (LCNC) with Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), marking a transformative era in product development. As organizations strive to accelerate innovation and reduce time-to-market, the synergy between LCNC and GenAI offers unprecedented opportunities for rapid prototyping, efficient development, and enhanced creativity. Finally, we look forward to how this convergence might reshape the landscape of product development, democratizing innovation, and the future of work for technology-driven sectors. This is done through research in both the literature review method and experimental methodology.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Techniques Applied to Intrusion Detection Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: As cyber threats continue to evolve, the necessity of Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) to protect sensitive information has become increasingly apparent. To address the limitations of conventional signature-based IDS, machine learning-based approaches have been proposed. However, the dearth of up-to-date network datasets impedes the advancement of these innovative methods. Furthermore, robust and reproducible results are required to ensure that the performance of ML models is not merely a product of randomness but a reflection of genuine and reliable capabilities. In this context, this paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of standalone and hybrid machine learning algorithms aimed at improving the differentiation between normal and malicious traffic. The hybrid model combines rule-based filtering with machine learning-based evaluation. A set of predefined rules is first applied to filter the dataset, and then the ML algorithms focus on the most relevant data, thus improving the efficiency in detecting previously unseen threats and reducing computational complexity. This approach is designed to improve detection accuracy while maintaining a low false positive rate, addressing both precision and operational efficiency in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Why should science fiction be learned in engineering education?
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This study explores the integration of science fiction in education, highlighting its potential as a powerful pedagogical tool in engineering and other scientific disciplines. By employing science fiction narratives and analogical models, complex concepts such as thermodynamics, energy, and entropy are made more accessible and engaging for students. The research demonstrates that science fiction can motivate students, promote active learning, and foster critical thinking. This interdisciplinary approach bridges the gap between theoretical principles and practical application, enriching the educational experience and preparing students to tackle real-world challenges with innovative solutions. The findings suggest that science fiction significantly enhances the educational process, contributing to the development of more competent and creative professionals.

articleTitle: Impact of Modeling Photovoltaic Power Plants Operating in Grid Forming Mode on Small-Signal Stability of Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The increased integration of photovoltaic (PV) power plants operating in grid-following (GFL) mode has raised concerns about small-signal stability. The grid-forming (GFM) mode appears to be a plausible solution to these issues, generating interest in studying the small-signal stability of power systems dominated by power electronic converters, such as those in PV plants. However, stability studies generally neglect the dynamic phenomena related to the DC-side, specifically the DC-DC converter and the PV, which can lead to inaccuracies. This work investigates the impact of modeling the DC-side of a PV power plant operating in GFM (PV-GFM) on the small-signal stability of a power system. Modal analysis is performed on a test system under various operating conditions, including PV-GFM plants and converter-interfaced generation (CIG) in GFM where the DC-side is neglected. The results show that oscillatory instabilities occur when the DC-side is modeled. On the other hand, the system performs better dynamically when CIG-GFM is considered. Additionally, the oscillatory characteristics of the modes change, and new systemic interactions appear. The findings demonstrate the significant impact of the DC-side dynamics of PV-GFM on small-signal stability and highlight the need for accurate representation.

articleTitle: Automated AirWellness System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Many Latin American countries face indoor air quality issues due to rapid urban growth, industrialization, and the lack of environmental regulations. Companies must ensure safe work environments in Tungurahua, Ecuador, especially concerning air quality. Exposure to $\mathrm{CO}, \mathrm{NOx}, \mathrm{SO}_{2}$, and particulate matter (PM) can lead to respiratory illnesses. This project focuses on mitigating air pollution in indoor spaces of companies in Tungurahua through an automated purification system using IoT. Employing automated measurement technology, the system identifies and manages chemical and ergonomic risks. An activated carbon-based purification system optimizes the reduction of pollutants, while IoT integration allows for real-time monitoring and automatic activation of the cleaner. The system’s validation was performed by quantifying alcohol ($2000 \mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$), carbon monoxide (100 ppm), carbon dioxide (200 ppm), and PM2.5 particles ($2500 \mathrm{ug} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$). A statistical analysis using the Wilcoxon test showed a significant difference between the values before and after using the purifier, with a p-value less than 0.05, allowing the rejection of the null hypothesis and acceptance of the alternative. The results indicate a significant reduction in pollution levels. This prototype can improve air quality in indoor spaces, promoting respiratory health among workers and providing a foundation for the development of future risk prevention systems.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network-based Classification of Parkinsonian Voice Disorders: A Spectrogram Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Parkinson’s disease produces a progressive degradation of motor (tremor, rigidity and slowness of movement) and non motor (cognitive, olfactory and speech) capabilities. Voice disorders are of great interest for patient monitoring and control, indeed as a possible predictor for early diagnosis of the disease. In this work, we implement three Deep Learning architectures to identify voice disorders associated with Parkinson’s disease from audio recordings. The audio records contain information on phonemes pronunciation and text reading. The proposed framework utilizes sliding windows to generate spectrograms for four ranges of frequencies. Then, the spectrograms are classified using a baseline convolutional neural network, ResNet50, and ResNet50V2. Results showed that the time of 2 seconds and spectral window range of $0-8000 \mathrm{~Hz}$ are the optimum settings to maximize the algorithm performance for both phonemes pronunciation and text reading. The experimental results showed that the proposed Resnet50v2 variant outperformed the other models, achieving a classification rate of $\mathbf{9 5 \%}$ for the phoneme classification, and $\mathbf{9 6. 6 7 \%}$ for the text classification. Results demonstrate that voice disorders in Parkinson’s disease can be accurately identified by the audio spectrograms using convolutional based architectures.

articleTitle: Integration of STEAM Competencies in the Development of IoT Components Through Social Media, Project-Based Learning (PBL), and the SAFe Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This article proposes an innovative methodology based on Project-Based Learning (PBL) and the agile SAFe framework for the development of technological components focused on the Internet of Things (IoT). Utilizing recent studies and effective learning strategies, this approach integrates theory and practice while fostering creativity, collaboration, and problem-solving among students. It emphasizes the development of STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics) competencies through the use of social media platforms, enhancing interaction and information exchange. Additionally, the article discusses how the implementation of the SAFe framework can improve the efficiency and quality of educational projects.

articleTitle: An integration proposal for heterogeneous industrial networking by using real-time processing in a programmable automation controller
