publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The continuous evolution of communication technologies has facilitated the modernization, automation, and digitalization of industrial networks. However, integrating new devices into existing networks can be challenging due to the diversity of communication protocols and components of the physical layer. This work presents a management model to address this issue by enabling the integration of various technologies into SCADA systems through a programmable automation controller (PAC) that utilizes the OPC protocol to handle communication heterogeneity. This paper describes crucial processes for improved interoperability and seamless information exchange in industrial networks. To validate and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solution, an industrial network of a microgrid laboratory is used as a practical application case. The study highlights the successful implementation of the solution, which makes it a suitable approach to improve the integration of technologies within industrial networks.

articleTitle: A brief review of the techniques used to locate electric bus charging stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Transit agencies are increasingly adopting battery electric buses (BEBs) and need to strategically place charging infrastructure to balance upfront costs and operational performance. This paper provides a robust introduction and explores options provided by artificial intelligence for optimal placement of charging stations. Subsequently, the identified algorithms and techniques are presented, as well as their respective validations. This paper presents a comprehensive review of more than 50 studies on electric bus charging station siting techniques. Optimization problems are identified that integrate factors such as site selection, station size, and the nonlinear battery charging process. The transition from conventional to electric buses requires developing adequate charging infrastructure, initially focused on large bus stations and now expanded to reduce crowding and delays at multi-port stations. The review emphasizes the importance of considering each country’s infrastructure and policies, international collaboration, development of supporting policies, investment in research and development, and adaptation to local needs to advance in this area. Suboptimal placement of charging stations can cause problems of autonomy and grid stability, underscoring the need for meticulous, data-driven planning.

articleTitle: Learning Service: Transforming Secondary Education
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of Learning Service on the teaching-learning process and the academic development of second-year high school students at the Ecuadorian Dutch Educational Unit during the academic year 2023-2024. A quantitative and descriptive approach was employed, using surveys and academic performance evaluations. The results show a significant improvement in students’ cognitive and psychosocial development, supported by a positive perception of teachers regarding the effectiveness of Learning Service. The conclusions highlight the importance of integrating innovative educational strategies that promote meaningful learning and students’ social engagement. Increased implementation of Learning Service in the school curriculum is recommended to strengthen students’ social and cognitive skills.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a Machine Learning-based Algorithm for AC Optimal Power Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Numerous efforts have been made to find efficient optimization methods that reduce resolution times to obtain solutions to the optimal power flow problem in alternating current (ACOPF). ACOPF is a non-convex and highly nonlinear problem. Power flow optimization problems (OPF) are usually solved using interior point methods, also known as barrier methods. One of the most commonly used approaches is the dual interior point method with filter line search. These methods are robust but expensive, as they require the calculation of the second derivative of the Lagrangian at each iteration. A promising research direction is utilizing machine learning (ML) techniques to solve operation and control problems in electrical networks. ML has been shown to significantly reduce the computational resources required in many real-world problems. Various solution methods have been employed, such as random forest, multi-objective decision tree, and extreme learning machine. In this case, ML is applied as a method that predicts voltage magnitudes and angles at each node, using physics-based network equations to calculate power injection at different nodes. For ML training, the data is divided into three sets: training, validation, and testing. These algorithms focus on minimizing their objective function and the operational cost of an AC transmission network.

articleTitle: Exploring the Role of Interactional & Procedural Justice in Preventing Moral Disengagement within an Organization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: To work well, employees need mental peace regarding the office environment and interpersonal relations. With increasing competitiveness in the corporate world, organizations are racing against each other to provide maximum output in minimum time, which may compromise occupational safety. The organization’s psychological safety climate, which includes mechanisms to provide justice to employees, has a long-term impact on employees’ decisionmaking skills. A dysfunctional justice system may lead to underreporting of safety risks and the development of a culture of moral disengagement and blatant disregard for rules. At time 1, data was collected from employees of manufacturing organizations [$\mathrm{n}=343$, response rate $=57 \%$], and at time 2 [n=220, response rate $=\mathbf{4 1 \%]}$. Partial Least Square, structural equation modeling technique was used to evaluate the proposed framework. Results showed a meaningful relationship between procedural justice and reporting attitude with safety moral disengagement. While interactional and procedural justice moderated the relationship between reporting attitude and safety moral disengagement but not with psychological safety climate. The study fills an important gap in the literature about the role of procedural and interactional justice with respect to workers’ moral disengagement from safety practices.

articleTitle: Enhancing Electric Power Consumption Prediction Using Machine Learning and Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Electric power consumption prediction enables the development of smart strategies aimed at conserving energy, enhancing efficiency, and establishing sensible pricing mechanisms. In this paper, we used predictive models for electric power consumption using machine learning and genetic algorithm techniques. The dataset utilized consists of socio-demographic instances and power consumption-related measured values collected by Centrales Eléctricas de Nariño (CEDENAR), Colombia. Three predictive models—Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM), and Support Vector Machines (SVM)—were employed to predict power consumption. Additionally, a genetic algorithm (GA) was applied to optimize the parameter values of each model. Performance metrics, including mean absolute error (MAE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), root mean squared error (RMSE), and coefficient of determination ($\mathrm{R}^{2}$), were used to evaluate the effectiveness of the models. Our findings indicate that all models, both in their standalone forms and after genetic algorithm optimization, demonstrate improvements in performance metrics. However, statistically, the RF + GA model exhibits superiority only in the MAE and MAPE metrics, achieving an $\mathrm{R}^{2}$ of 0.76, reflecting its enhanced predictive capability in electric power consumption estimation. These results offer valuable insights for energy management strategies and resource planning in the context of electricity consumption.

articleTitle: ARCHIE: Articulated Robot for Collaborative Highly Integrated Education
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Articulated robots, known for their versatility and precision, play a fundamental role in educational and research environments. This paper presents the design, implementation, and evaluation of a 6-degree-of-freedom robotic arm, using Dynamixel motors, aimed at providing a cost-effective and robust solution. The design of the robotic arm incorporates precise control through the Robot Operating System (ROS) and motion planning with MoveIt, ensuring accurate task execution. As part of the development process, a detailed 3D model and a Gazebobased simulation were created, allowing thorough testing and refinement in a virtual environment before physical deployment. The complete documentation, including a parts list and open-source code, is available in a GitHub repository. The results of this project demonstrate significant potential to improve educational experiences in mechatronics and to advance research capabilities, establishing this robotic arm as a valuable tool for academic and experimental purposes.

articleTitle: Gamification for psychomotor development: an experience with Genially in pre-school education
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Psychomotor skills in early childhood are notably affected due to the pandemic, which is why the objective of the research was to implement gamified strategies in Genially that seek to improve psychomotor development in early education, the research had a mixed and field approach, with a proposal in which 21 students participated for 4 weeks; before the application of the proposal and after it, tests were applied, where the results obtained fulfilled the expectations of improvement in the teaching process.

articleTitle: Enhancing QoS in Urban V2V Communications Through AI: A Machine Learning Approach in Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This study introduces a machine learning-based Quality of Service (QoS) model that significantly enhances Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communications within urban vehicular networks. To validate our model, we compared its performance against the conventional Enhanced Distributed Channel Access (EDCA) mechanism and a scenario without QoS enhancements. Simulations were conducted in an urban area of Buenos Aires, Argentina. We utilized Open Street Maps (OSM) to provide a realistic geographic foundation, ensuring our simulation environment closely mirrors actual urban settings. SUMO (Simulation of Urban Mobility) was employed to accurately model vehicular movements and interactions, facilitating a dynamic and realistic traffic flow simulation. The ns-3 (Network Simulator 3) was used for the network communication aspects, simulating complex network protocols and interactions with high fidelity. Together, these tools enabled comprehensive testing of the QoS model, highlighting its capacity to improve packet delivery ratio (PDR), reduce end-to-end delays, and enhance received throughput. The results underscore the potential of machine learning to significantly optimize vehicular network communications, paving the way for more efficient and reliable urban transportation systems.

articleTitle: Software Architecture and Simulation Interface for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: In the cutting-edge field of unmanned underwater vehicles, advanced simulation, and software architecture are essential parts for the innovation and scalable development of any project. This paper presents a robust and modular software architecture for simulating an AUV, integrating current technologies with strong community support such as ROS2 Humble, Gazebo, and Rviz for deep immersion in controlled environment simulation. Through meticulous algorithm development for navigation and teleoperation, this research paves the way for implementing future control and detection strategies that transcend current engineering challenges. The results demonstrate a clear and robust software architecture that accurately simulates AUV Max operations, marking progress in the development of future underwater explorations. This paper invites readers to delve into our architecture, addressing software implications to ensure scalability over time.

articleTitle: Towards Sustainable Development Based on University Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Electricity is indeed a fundamental element of contemporary society, and the transition towards ensuring clean and affordable electrical energy is one of the present challenges. This transition has proved to progress slowly, primarily due to the challenges associated with integrating renewable distributed energy resources (DERs). For instance, weather changes can dramatically impact the amount of peak power supplied on any given day. Microgrids are a promising concept that can help address these challenges, and many studies can be found in the literature that focus on implementing these complex systems. However, there is a gap in the literature regarding the specific subject of using the infrastructure of universities as a proof-of-concept. This paper aims to help fill this gap by reporting the case study of the University of Campinas (UNICAMP), in Brazil. The paper summarizes the current research in the local microgrid of UNICAMP, and shows its potential to boost sustainable development by decarbonizing universities, as a practical contribution beyond their educational value. The main components of the system are described, and the presented numerical results show how at least 33% of the campus’s monthly electricity consumption can be reduced. This proves that real-world microgrids can have a positive impact, not only on greenhouse gas emissions reduction but also on the overall system efficiency.

articleTitle: EPOLARIS: A tool for active Wide Area Network Automation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Traditional CLI-driven network management needs to be faster and prone to human error. Besides, Wide Area Network operation is complex and challenging due to the number of devices. Network programmability allows for automating network configurations and troubleshooting, reducing response time and increasing business agility. This work presents the EPOLARIS tool intended to facilitate and improve WAN network management. It provides real-time network monitoring and automation, proactive tasks and automated alerts and notifications. The EPOLARIS tool has been evaluated in simulated and real-world scenarios, demonstrating enhanced network management and easy usage. The tool allows for smaller equipment configuration time and faster detection of topology errors. Besides, an expanded view of network device interconnections enhances problem-solving robustness. Besides, notifications combined with pre-event network analysis facilitate incident response time.

articleTitle: An Application Layer Protocol for the Transmission of Hydrometeorological Data over LoRaWAN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have been increasingly deployed in hydrometeorological stations to enhance the collection and transmission of environmental data. LoRa-based Wireless Sensor Networks is a wireless communication protocol between nodes or sensors. This work proposes an application layer protocol, Variable Meteorological Transmission Protocol VMTPv2, for transmitting hydrometeorological data. The proposed protocol is based on the application layer level’s VMTP version 1. Additionally, this work implements the VMTPv2 protocol explicitly designed to work on LoRaWAN using LoRa nodes and Gateway. The experimental results show that the proposed application protocol significantly reduces energy consumption in nodes by at least 30% and 90% in the Gateway compared to the Cayenne LPP and VMTPv1 protocols.

articleTitle: Innovation Strategies for Training Management with STEAM, IoT, and AI through Design Thinking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This study addresses the implementation of an innovative learning strategy that integrates the STEAM methodology, the Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI). within the field of robotics teaching, using Design Thinking as a catalyst. It delves into how the combination of these disciplines can enrich engineering education, promoting an interactive, creative and student-centered approach to the development of IoT prototypes. The research highlights the need to adapt curricula to include these advanced technologies, which is essential to train students in creating innovative IoT solutions that respond to the demands of the current and future technological landscape.

articleTitle: Emotion-Based Interaction Mode Selection Model for University Students
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: User interaction is one of the biggest concerns for designers, programmers, and engineers since the user decides the acceptance of a technological solution, so the user must feel comfortable with the created solution. Since few studies adapt technology to users, it is necessary to conduct a study on user preferences to understand their bases. This work develops a validated survey to identify the demographic, technological, and expertise characteristics that influence a student’s affective state according to a given interaction mode. This survey goes hand in hand with a model that predicts the emotional variables that a user will have when using one of these modes in order to obtain the emotional state of the person when using a specific device. A unique methodology was developed by combining an experimental process with CRISP DM and integrating its final steps to jointly create the survey and the model. The study included 64 university students who participated in a survey in which demographic, preference, and technological expertise data were collected. Participants’ performance and affective states (valence, dominance, and arousal) were measured during their interactions with each device. Significant correlations between personal characteristics, performance, and affective states were identified for each device used. We also obtained the characteristics that influence the person’s affective state and trained a model capable of predicting the affective variables with a sufficient amount of data.

articleTitle: A Data Quality Model and an Evaluation Method for Health Data in Ecuador
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Data represents an organization’s most important asset; hence, data engineers must ensure that its storage and processing methods comply with quality specifications that ensure its accuracy, confidentiality, and other quality attributes that allow it to be used fully. Although there are many software quality models, they are disjointed from the quality of the data being handled. Likewise, there is a lot of talk about the quality of information, but only some contributions align with a formal standard and regulations. Consequently, this article presents a data quality model aligned with ISO 25012 and Ecuador’s personal data protection law to serve as a tool for establishing dataset quality. Finally, using the quality model is exemplified through an evaluation process aligned with ISO 25040.

articleTitle: Beyond 5G: Comprehensive Radio Network Coverage/Capacity Planning for Subway Station Indoor scenario using RIS/Massive MIMO
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The deployment of 5G networks has improved indoor coverage, especially in subway stations. However, these environments pose challenges due to their complexity, high user density, signal losses, and costs of distributed antenna systems (DAS). This paper presents a beyond 5G (B5G) methodology for network planning using reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) and massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antennas in sub- 6 GHz and mmW ave frequencies, adhering to ETSI standards, and considering that sub- 6 GHz has greater coverage and penetration than mmWave. Detailed planning and simulations for La Pradera Metro station in Quito were conducted using the 5G indoor-hotspot (In-H) model and validated with Winprop. Our results show enhanced coverage/capacity over $191.75 \mathrm{~m}^{2}$, achieving peak throughput between 2.34 and 4.73 Gbps, significantly improving user service quality. This paper provides advanced indoor network design methodologies, offering insights for future 5G and B5G implementations.

articleTitle: FANET Networks: Analysis of Routing Protocols
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The evolution Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks from early ad-hoc communication networks to sophisticated Flying Ad-hoc Networks (FANETs) demonstrates significant progress. FANETs support massive deployments, rapid topology changes, configurable, and fault tolerance. This paper analyzes the performance of various routing algorithms-OLSR, DSDV, AODV, DSR, AOMDV, and HWMP-through simulations in NS3. The study evaluates these algorithms based on throughput, packet delivery ratio (PDR), and average delay under different scenarios: UAVs in static positions, UAVs flying at maximum speeds of $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and $20 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, with tests conducted using 25 and 50 UAVs. The results provide insights into the efficiency of these protocols in static and dynamic environments, offering valuable information for the design and optimization of UAV communication networks.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of Recycled Asphalt Pavement Combined with Crushed Glass, Cevallos-Mocha Road, Tungurahua, Ecuador
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The design of hot mix asphalt mixtures using recycled materials such as glass and asphalt pavement (RAP) represents a significant environmental contribution and constitutes an innovation in sustainable road construction. Objective: To analyze the behavior of hot asphalt mixtures in the face of the partial substitution of different percentages of crushed glass and recycled asphalt pavement (RAP) in the structure of the asphalt mixture as a reinforcement element for use in the design of sustainable roads. Methodology: The research was divided into three phases. In the first phase, bibliographic information from studies carried out in the study route and on the incorporation of recycled materials such as glass and recycled asphalt pavement in hot bituminous mixtures was analyzed. In the second phase, alternatives for the design of hot asphalt mixtures were formulated, partially replacing crushed glass and recycled asphalt pavement in its structure. In the final phase, the master formula of the asphalt mixture was established that met all the Marshall criteria and additionally incorporated crushed glass and recycled asphalt pavement in its structure. General Area of Study: Civil Engineering. Specific area of study: Pavement Engineering.

articleTitle: Leveraging Deep Learning Techniques for Marine and Coastal Wildlife Using Instance Segmentation: A Study on Galápagos Sea Lions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Instance segmentation is a powerful deep learning technique that goes beyond traditional object detection by identifying and delineating individual objects within an image. This study evaluates several algorithms for instance segmentation of sea lions from video frames captured in the Galápagos Islands. The YOLO v8 and v9 models demonstrated superior metric values compared to other models, including those based on Detectron2 with a Mask R-CNN backbone. The study addressed challenges such as species proximity during group activities, variability in lighting conditions and image quality. YOLO v8 achieved an average precision (AP50) rate of 97.90%, while YOLO v9 achieved a precision rate of 98.2% for sea lion instance segmentation. These results provide valuable resources for future analysis of wildlife monitoring methods across diverse natural environments, with significant implications for conservation.

articleTitle: Performance and Real-World Variability of Predictive Maintenance Models for Vehicle Fleets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive evaluation of predictive maintenance models for vehicle fleets, detailing a sequence of systematic steps to ensure model performance and address real-world variability. The process begins with database creation and data preprocessing, where relevant maintenance records are filtered, and datetime columns are converted to facilitate time-based calculations. Grouping and aggregation techniques are then applied to count occurrences of specific maintenance activities and identify common failure types. For model training, we define a neural network architecture comprising dense and dropout layers to mitigate overfitting, compile the model with suitable loss functions and optimizers, and train it using the prepared data. The trained model, along with the scaler and encoder, is saved for future use. To augment the dataset, synthetic data is generated using the Faker library and random distributions, with added noise to mimic real-world variability. Preprocessing steps are reapplied to this synthetic data to ensure consistency. By implementing this neural network, we achieved a sensitivity of 0.93 and an ROC of 0.71. Following these detailed steps, we develop a robust predictive maintenance model that effectively identifies failures and non-failures, ultimately enhancing the reliability and efficiency of vehicle fleet management.

articleTitle: Generative AI and the Future of Interactive and Immersive Advertising
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Generative AI is revolutionizing interactive and immersive advertising by enabling more personalized, engaging experiences through advanced technologies like VR, AR, and MR. This transformation is reshaping how advertisers create, deliver, and optimize content, allowing for two-way communication and blurring lines between digital and physical worlds. AI enhances user engagement through predictive analytics, real-time adaptation, and natural language processing, while also optimizing ad placement and personalization. Future trends include integration with emerging technologies like $\mathbf{5 G}$ and IoT, fully immersive experiences, and hyper-personalization. However, challenges such as privacy concerns, transparency issues, and ethical considerations must be addressed. As AI continues to evolve, it promises to create unprecedented opportunities for brands to connect with audiences in meaningful ways, potentially blurring the line between advertising and interactive entertainment. The industry must proactively address these challenges to ensure AI-driven advertising enhances user experiences while respecting privacy and maintaining trust.

articleTitle: State of the art of the automatized characterization of chronic wound patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Currently, medicine has experienced a growing interest in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) combined with other information technologies, for the interpretation, classification and prediction of pathologies and injuries from medical images in an automated or semi-automated way because they contribute, among other tasks, to diagnose and monitor patients. This work is a systematic review of five databases exploring projects, between 2018 and 2024, that have used Artificial Intelligence techniques like deep learning and machine learning in the classification, segmentation, and detection of wound images. The results suggest that these technologies in the medical field can reduce workload, standardize diagnosis, improve accuracy and treatment, and positively impact the quality of patient care. The management of chronic wounds is complex due to their etiology and the lack of visual capacity of the medical professional. For this reason, the automation of these processes promises to have the potential to significantly improve medical care, and consequently, affect the quality of patients’ lives.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis for Traffic Officer Detection in Autonomous Vehicles using YOLOv3, v5, and v8
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This article focuses on generating an alternative to identify traffic officers during driving. This research employed the You Only Look Once (YOLO) model, using a sixphase methodology: data collection, data preparation involving resizing and labeling, implementation of various filters to avoid overfitting, model training, prediction evaluation, and result interpretation. The YOLO model was applied across three iterations using a dataset of 1862 images. The graphics processing unit (GPU) acceleration was utilized to enhance training efficiency and detection speed, further enhancing the experimental process. The results of this study revealed that the YOLOv8x variant produced the most promising results. This proposed model attained a remarkable F1 score of 0.95, bolstered by a confidence score of 0.631, with the potential to increase to 0.80 in confidence without significantly compromising the F1-score. These findings are poised to contribute substantially to the broader research landscape, particularly in advancing the effectiveness of detection models for traffic officers.

articleTitle: On the assessment of reinforcement learning techniques for trayectory tracking of autonomous ground robots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This study investigates the application of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) techniques in the trajectory tracking control of autonomous mobile robots. Assessing control performance under model parameter variations and disturbances, this work evaluates the suitability of DRL for a more adaptable and robust navigation solution. It was evaluated Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) and Twin-Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) techniques to identify their strengths and limitations when using information of real-time dynamics, whereas a Model Predictive control (MPC) strategy is incorporated to contrast robust performance when using uncertain prediction models. The DDPG approach effectively learns complex policies for trajectory tracking but requires a careful balance between exploration and exploitation, and it has limited adaptability to environmental changes. In contrast, TD3 outperforms DDPG and NMPC in terms of trajectory tracking error and control effort across different model uncertainties and disturbances. This work highlights the potential for future research to enhance DRL-based controllers, particularly in handling uncertainties and disturbances during autonomous navigation tasks.

articleTitle: Evaluation and opportunities for energy savings in a company in the telecommunications sector using ISO 50 001
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: In the last decade our planet has been declared in a climate emergency caused by the environmental impacts associated with different industrial activities and the inefficient use of energy. The telecommunications sector is no stranger to this reality, its growing energy demand is directly related to the increase in greenhouse gas emissions. Through ISO 50 001: 2018, energy efficiency is considered the second alternative to mitigate environmental impacts and improve the efficient use of energy in different industries worldwide. This descriptive research develops the energy planning phase in a company of the telecommunications sector in Cuba. The areas of higher consumption were identified by means of Pareto diagrams for energy sources, control diagrams for consumption and production, an energy baseline is proposed and the energy performance indicator is determined. The energy carriers of electricity and diesel were the most representative with $85 \%$ of total consumption, the area with the highest consumption of electricity is associated with the second administrative floor with $75.34 \%$, air conditioners represent $66.44 \%$ of the total consumption of electricity in the company. A baseline is established by relating the $\mathrm{kWh} / \mathrm{m} 2 * \mathrm{DG}$ indicator. The energy reduction proposal is through an analysis of the replacement of 350 fluorescent tubes with LED technology to reduce by $1,190.24$ $\mathrm{kWh} /$ month and ${\$}$2,856.34 per year, for a payback period of 1.3 years. Energy efficiency is the sustainable alternative to have an efficient use of energy in the telecommunications sector and reduce environmental impacts.

articleTitle: Bioremediation of Soils Contaminated With Hydrocarbons and Heavy Metals, Huancavelica
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The objective of this study is to analyze the effect of sunflower (Helianthus anuuss L) and wheat (Triticum aestivum L) and the addition of organic amendments (guinea pig manure and sawdust) on soil contaminated by metals and hydrocarbons. For this purpose, 15 pots of 10 kg of soil and a 2:1 distribution (soil and amendment) were prepared. The design was completely randomized, with a $2 \times 2$ factorial arrangement with 6 treatments and 3 replicates, for 6 months. Slight increases in $\mathrm{PH}, \mathrm{OM}$ and CE were determined due to the addition of amendments and exudates of the plant species. The highest TPH removal was achieved with wheat-guinea pig extract, with a 26% reduction. The highest removal of $\mathbf{C d}$, (77%) $\mathbf{C u }$ (33.3%), P b (85.9%) and Zn(87.9%)was with the plant species (Wheat/Girasol)-no amendment. The plant species had a greater impact on the removal of heavy metals, while the organic amendments reduced the presence of hydrocarbons and improved the physical properties of the soil.

articleTitle: Open Source Geospatial tools for Solar Atlas in a Thermal and Photovoltaic Analysis applied to Cuenca-Ecuador
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This paper introduces the development of a solar atlas designed to evaluate both photovoltaic and thermal energy potentials in urban environments. The study focuses on Las Herrerias sector in Cuenca, Ecuador, detailing data inputs, software tools, and methodologies employed. It provides a granular view of solar radiation incidence by integrating geospatial data and highresolution orthophotos. Key formulas for estimating solar electric output and thermal efficiency are applied. The findings underscore the importance of utilizing localized data for renewable energy projects, highlighting areas with the highest potential for solar energy exploitation. Additionally, the integration of shadow mapping identifies optimal rooftops for solar panel installation.

articleTitle: A Scoping Review and Bibliometric Analysis of Strategies for Teaching Electrical Circuits in Secondary School
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Electrical circuits are a central topic in natural science curricula at the secondary education level. The abstract nature of electricity makes this subject particularly challenging for high school students. This article combines a scoping review and bibliometric analysis to map and analyze the literature on teaching strategies for electrical circuits in high school. Moreover, it explores successful practices and exemplary cases that have positively influenced student 1 earning in this area. Overall, this study enhances our understanding of effective methods for improving the instruction of electrical circuits in secondary education.

articleTitle: Identification of construction project failure factors and development of a Predictive model for evaluation of contractors in public procurement of construction works
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The development of infrastructure, being a primary developmental need of a state, consumes a major portion of a country’s GDP, through public procurements. Globally, public procurement accounts for fifteen percent (15%) of total expenditures. Among these, the procurement of construction works is particularly substantial, estimated at approximately 10 trillion dollars annually. The construction industry alone contributes to approximately ten percent (10%) of the world’s gross domestic product (GDP). However, it has been reported that a significant proportion of construction projects ultimately result in failure. Three primary issues commonly associated with construction projects are overrunning project deadlines, exceeding budgeted costs, and failing to meet quality standards. The majority of these issues in construction projects are experienced during the execution phase, with contactors reported as being a major source of these anomalies. This observation is substantiated by ranking of construction project failure factors using the relative importance indexing method and finding the prominence values through Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory technique. The results of the ranking and prominence values highlights that the selection of an incompetent contractor and financial challenges faced by the contractor are the most critical factors contributing to project failure. Therefore, it is imperative to select a competent and suitable contractor for construction works in order to reduce the risk of failure. To address this issue, the research is currently in the conceptual stage, embarking a novel approach to construct a machine learning model. This model, developed using historical data from completed construction projects, aims to serve as a predictive tool for evaluating and selecting a suitable contractor. Through the utilization of artificial intelligence and historical data analysis, the model is intended not only to enhance decision-making for procurement management but also to identify areas where contractors can make improvements.

articleTitle: Assessing the Impact of Frequency Stability Constraints in Generation Expansion Planning with Variable Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The rapid shift to inertia-less variable renewable energy (VRE) technologies is displacing many synchronous generators (SGs), reducing frequency support and inertial response, and significantly affecting system frequency dynamics. Therefore, at high levels of VRE penetration, it is crucial to accurately represent frequency stability constraints in power system operation and planning. This paper presents a two-stage methodology to assess the impact of frequency stability constraints in the generation expansion planning (GEP) model, focusing on VRE integration and the dynamic performance of power systems. The first stage involves the GEP model determining the optimal new generation capacity mix, considering linearized frequency stability constraints. The second stage assesses the GEP results’ dynamic performance by simulating power system transients using DIgSILENT PowerFactory. To quantify the impact of frequency stability constraints, we consider three security indices: initial rate of change of frequency (RoCoF), frequency nadir, and steady-state frequency deviation. Finally, we analyze two case studies: the GEP model with and without considering frequency constraints on an illustrative 13-bus test system. The results demonstrate that integrating frequency constraints into the GEP problem results in higher system inertia, leading to significant improvements in the security indices but a more expensive investment in generation portfolios.

articleTitle: An immersive system for light vehicles in entertainment apps using virtual reality
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Nowadays, virtual reality has many innovative applications in the engineering field. The present w ork focuses on developing an integrated virtual reality system for entertainment using light vehicles for indoor cycling to generate an immersive experience. The methodology is based on the next stages: 1) the user operation for direct interaction with the system; 2) the data acquisition using sensors to process them through the ESP32 development board; 3) the simulation and communication using MQTT protocol between software and hardware, generating variations in the physical and virtual environment; 4) the motor control to generate the resistance to movement through simulator roller according to the changes in the virtual environment. Finally, 5) the mobile app to view and save speed, slope, and time variables collected during an active session. According to the results, the localhost MQTT broker is the most stable server for connecting different devices in 10 milliseconds. The maximum latency between ESP32 and Unity is 6.01 milliseconds. The real speed of movement correlates 0.999 with the speed measured by the sensor and generated in a virtual environment. According to the survey, the level of satisfaction with using the immersive system is around 91%, on the Likert scale. Compared with a commercial system, it is a low-cost alternative for this type of application because the cost has been reduced to about 53%. Future work is focused on developing an immersive system for remote tourism and rehabilitation for disabled people applications.

articleTitle: Promoting Ethics in Engineering: an Approach Based on Student Competitions. Case of Ecuador
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Education in ethics plays a fundamental role in the preparation of engineers, who must be prepared to face moral questions when making decisions in their professional practice. However, the lack of engineering ethics education persists in some countries, posing significant challenges i n the training of ethically responsible professionals. Therefore, this research describes a case study of an ethics competition as a pedagogical approach that combines the study of professional codes of ethics, analysis of case studies and oral debates. A quasi-experimental design with a nonequivalent control group is used to evaluate the effectiveness of the Engineering Ethics Competence, measured through a pre- and post-test questionnaire that assesses knowledge and commitment to professional ethics. Regarding the results, a significant improvement is observed in the participants’ knowledge and commitment to ethics, specifically in their ability to apply ethical principles in practical engineering situations, in their awareness of the importance of ethics in their careers, the ability to recognize ethical dilemmas and the perception of the relevance of ethical codes.

articleTitle: First steps to create a data-driven culture in organizations. Case study in a financial institution.
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The purpose of this article is to identify the practice of communicating with data as a central axis for the development of a data-driven culture in organizations. Currently, communicating using data through graphs and symbols is a daily practice in organizations that seek to obtain value from it to base their decisions, even in departments and among people who do not necessarily have statistical or mathematical knowledge. This article analyzes the behavior of the risk department of an organization that belongs to the Colombian financial system under the case study methodology, considering group literacy as the first step in the data communication activity. Subsequently, it is observed and deepened through in-depth interviews in relation to the change in the organizational practices of the group of leaders and managers of the organization. As a result of the study, the existence of a relationship between data-driven communication and organizational cultural practices is established through an experimental model for measuring data-driven culture. Although measuring data culture in an organization is not a task with a solid scientific basis yet, there are efforts aimed at measuring the analytical maturity of organizations under some development models, which seek to identify these capabilities. In conclusion, the study identifies a positive relationship between data communication and organizational cultural practices, contributing significantly to the development of a data-driven culture.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning-Based Methods for Multivariate Time Series Imputation with Varying Missing Rates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Multivariate Time Series (MTS), pervasive in fields such as industry and healthcare, enable the understanding of time-dependent phenomena, leading to better predictions, more effective interventions, and improved decision-making across various applications. A common issue in MTS is missing data, which arises from diverse sampling mechanisms, ranging from malfunctioning sensors to medical exams conducted at different time intervals. Given that missing data in MTS can jeopardize downstream tasks such as forecasting and classification, numerous methods have been developed to address data imputation in MTS. However, a comparative analysis of these data imputation methods across varying missing rates is still needed. In this work, we compared five commonly used deep learning-based imputation methods (M-RNN, US-GAN, GP-VAE, SAITS, and BRITS) on the well-known Physionet Challenge 2012 dataset considering different percentages of missing data. Our results showed that SAITS exhibited the lowest average error while BRITS demonstrated lower error dispersion.

articleTitle: Evaluation of 5G Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) Communications in Urban Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This paper presents a simulation and evaluation of vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication within a real urban environment tailored for fifth-generation (5G) networks. The main contributions are: (i) utilizing a real map segment of Barcelona, Spain, from OpenStreetMap; (ii) generating vehicular mobility patterns using the Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) tool; and (iii) simulating vehicular communications with the ns-3 network simulator. The study employs the 3GPP Urban Macro (UMa) propagation model to accurately represent the urban communication conditions of 5G V2X, accounting for obstacles like buildings and foliage. Various scenarios, both with and without specific communication patterns, are compared to assess their impact on key metrics, such as the average packet inter-reception rate and packet reception rate, revealing notable differences in variability and effectiveness. The use of cumulative distribution functions (CDFs) further illustrates the impact of urban obstacles on 5G V2X communications. An iterative simulation approach is adopted to automatically optimize model parameters, thereby improving the robustness of the results and their practical applicability.

articleTitle: Data-centric Competencies through Professional Certification: Understanding the Gap between Industry and Undergraduate Data Science Education
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The digital revolution has transformed industries, making data science pivotal for strategic decision-making. This shift requires a close alignment between university curricula and industry needs to adequately prepare graduates for the challenges of a data-driven economy. This study, through a pilot survey of IT professionals, master’s and undergraduate students in data analytics in Ecuador and Poland, investigates the gap between current academic programs and practical industry requirements. Preliminary findings indicate a robust consensus on the value of professional certifications for career advancement and highlight a growing demand for competencies in data analytics and artificial intelligence, especially in Ecuador. Challenges such as the lack of practical applications and the discrepancy between educational content and business realities are noted. In response, this paper proposes a motivation model that integrates professional certifications into data science curricula to enhance employability, competitiveness, and adaptability. This model emphasizes the importance of soft skills and the recognition of certifications in the business sphere. By addressing the specific needs and expectations of industry professionals, this study contributes to the discourse on refining data science education, aiming to bridge the academic-industry gap and equip graduates with the essential competencies needed for success in the dynamic IT landscape.

articleTitle: Cost-Effective Gamma Radiation Detection System for Environmental Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This research presents the design and implementation of a cost-effective radiation detection system using a Geiger-Muller tube. The system includes a high-voltage circuit, nuclear pulse conditioning, and SCADA integration for real-time data acquisition. The design process utilized Proteus for simulation and ensured optimal component layout. Implementation results confirmed the system’s reliability and accuracy in detecting gamma radiation, underscoring its importance for environmental monitoring and safety. The system provides an efficient and affordable solution for ionizing radiation detection.

articleTitle: An experimental comparison of model-based fault detection and isolation techniques in a multi-tank system
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Fault detection and isolation (FDI) systems ensure processes’ safety, reliability, and secure operation. Many techniques proposed in the literature work well in simulation scenarios, but perform poorly in realistic systems with significant noise. This work presents a hybrid-based technique that uses an extended Kalman filter to smooth out measurements and parameter estimation of a nonlinear second-order model for quantifying leakage faults in an interconnected multi-tank system. The cost function for parameter estimation minimizes the squared error between predictions and measurements. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid technique yielded a better estimate than the baseline FDI techniques. The proposed technique improved the prediction of tank dynamics and fault estimation quality by about $\mathbf{3 2 \%}$.

articleTitle: A Literature Review on Enterprise Credit Assessment Using Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This article presents a literature review on enterprise credit assessment using the Random Forest model, distinguishing it from general credit assessment, which includes a broader range of entities. The study highlights the limitations of traditional methods in credit risk evaluation. The primary objective of this research is to assess the technical configurations, predictive capabilities, and ethical considerations of applying Random Forest in credit assessment. Methodologically, a literature review approach guided by PRISMA principles was adopted, focusing on relevant studies published between 2018 and 2024. The findings indicate that Random Forest models enhance predictive accuracy and effectively manage high-dimensional data, outperforming traditional statistical methods. Furthermore, the study emphasizes the need for transparency and bias mitigation in automated credit scoring systems.

articleTitle: A Shallow Approach for Vehicle Speed Estimation in Urban Areas Using YOLO, GOG, and a MLP
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: Modern traffic is a c omplex c hallenge of a ll urban areas around the globe. The complex nature of traffic m akes it necessary to use specialized tools to understand this phenomenon. Detection, tracking, and speed estimation are computational tools that help understand traffic, providing the necessary insights to design intelligent cities. These three tasks help predict vehicle flow and extract essential information for decision-making and city planning. This paper proposes a system with three components to estimate the speed of vehicles from video of urban scenes. The first c omponent p rocesses t he v ideo f rames u sing t he You Only Look Once (YOLO) algorithm for vehicle detection. The second component uses the Globally-Optimal Greedy Algorithm (GOG) to track the vehicles. Lastly, the third component is a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) that predicts vehicle speed based on differences from frame to frame. Our proposed system was tested by estimating vehicle speed in real and complex scenes to obtain a deeper insight into the behavior of the vehicles. The system is robust enough to work with different car types, light conditions, weather conditions, and camera positions. This paper presents our proposal, shows the experiments, and compares it with similar studies. Also, we draw conclusions and provide directions for future research.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Virtualized Control Systems Laboratory Experiments for Hybrid University Classes.
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This work presents a virtual laboratory experiment for control systems design at ESPOL, an Ecuadorian polytechnic university. After the COVID-19 pandemic, hybrid classes (i.e., in-presence, and virtual students at the same time) are one of the alternatives for ESPOL courses including the Advanced Control class. In this sense, laboratory experiments that are part of the course are difficult to run for virtual students since they are not able to observe the dynamic behavior of experiments. For this purpose, the selected plant is a three interconnected tanks system, from which a dynamic model is derived including the computation of model parameters relying on simple physical metrics, such as ball valve rotation angles. The model is properly validated through comparison with real data. A graphical interface is designed to illustrate the PID control systems design through direct manipulation of the tuning parameters, resembling a process that is common in control engineering practice. Finally, results from a survey among students are presented, to illustrate the perception and effectiveness of the proposed experiment.

articleTitle: Impact of Data Augmentation Using SMOTE and GAN on Machine Learning Predictions for Vehicular Routing Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of imbalanced datasets in Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs). We introduce a methodology comparing the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Networks (CTGANs) to balance our dataset, which is derived from complex simulations using OMNET++, SUMO, OpenStreetMaps, and Veins. This approach enabled the creation of synthetic data that accurately reflects essential routing metrics, significantly reducing the need for additional time-consuming simulations to increase the dataset. Through the employment of T-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (T-SNE), we assessed the quality of our augmented data and identified the most critical routing metrics using L1 regularization. These insights were crucial for optimizing our neural networks with the Hyperband algorithm. We compared these results with the neural network model from previous work, known as the Multimetric Predictive ANN-based Routing Protocol (MPANN), demonstrating improvements in the model’s performance even with a reduced number of metrics, as evidenced by gains in AUC, precision, F1-Score, and Cohen’s kappa. Moreover, our findings suggest a pathway for future implementation in urban vehicular network simulation environments.

articleTitle: Enhancement of an Adaptive Building-Skin System for Local and Remote Multi-Modal Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: This paper details the enhancement of a previously presented adaptive building-skin system consisting of independent-yet-interrelated context-aware components in a Cyber-Physical Network (CPN). The present development subsumes and extends the inherited services and capabilities— both mechanical and computational—of the previous system as follows. With respect to the mechanical: a second actuatable layer is integrated along the inherited first layer, which enables ventilation and natural-light intake to be determined independently via separate automatic or manual aperture controls. With respect to the computational: both local and remote, human and non-human multi-modal control / operation is integrated. More specifically, the following three new operation mechanisms are added along the inherited local sensor-based automatic mode: a local manual control-override based on (1) specific desired-aperture values (via a graphical slider) or (2) approximate desired-aperture values (via gyroscopic sensing) both based on Open Sound Control (OSC); and (3) a remote manual and/or automatic control-override based on Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT). The first two mechanisms involve local user interaction via a smart-device, and the third mechanism involves remote human and/or non-human interaction via if-this-then-that (IFTTT) and/or Adafruit IO cloud services. The objective of the enhanced adaptive building-skin system remains the intelligent interfacing between interior and exterior environments in a way that is conducive to user comfort, well-being, and environmental safety. Accordingly, the system is conceived as part of the intelligent built-environment discourse that integrates the technical / technological sophistication of Ambient Intelligence (AmI) / Active and Assisted Living (AAL) advances while remaining informed by Architectural considerations.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Wireless Communication Protocols for Lower-Limb Exoskeleton Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Eighth Ecuador Technical Chapters Meeting (ETCM)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness of three wireless communication methods in the context of a lower-limb exoskeleton system, comparing ESP-NOW in broadcast mode, traditional UDP/IP, and communication using Imocap-GIS devices. For this purpose, four different experimental architectures were designed, each comprising a controller (Jetson Nano) and a variable number of slave devices (nodes). The results indicate that ESP-NOW exhibited significantly lower latency times than UDP, positioning it as potentially more suitable for applications in wireless personal area networks that demand fast response times, such as real-time control systems. The experimental findings conclude that the ESP-NOW transmission protocol is prone to increased packet loss as the network expands, especially when the number of nodes increases from one to four, with a maximum loss of 8.6%. These observations emphasize the critical role of protocol selection, tailored to the application’s specific requirements and the network environment’s intricacies, in ensuring the reliability and efficiency of wireless communication systems.
